new_entities.name: Oral finasteride in men
new_entities.description: Oral finasteride therapy used in male androgenetic alopecia.

edges.effect_quant: A 48-week placebo-controlled trial in 212 men found finasteride produced a placebo-adjusted gain of 17.3 total hairs and 27 anagen hairs in the target scalp area. Larger comparative data and network meta-analysis continue to rank 1 mg finasteride among the most effective established male AGA monotherapies.
edges.population: adult men with androgenetic alopecia treated with oral finasteride, typically 1 mg daily
edges.mechanism: Finasteride lowers scalp dihydrotestosterone by inhibiting type II 5-alpha reductase, slowing follicular miniaturization and improving anagen maintenance in susceptible scalp hair.
edges.summary: Oral finasteride remains one of the most effective evidence-backed pharmacologic options for male pattern hair loss. The literature consistently shows meaningful improvement in hair density and anagen status, even if response is not uniform and long-term tradeoffs matter.
edges.caveats: This edge is about hair efficacy only, not the sexual-side-effect controversy, which belongs on a separate harms edge. Continued use is required to maintain benefit.

evidence.citation: VanNesteD et al 2000 Br J Dermatol
evidence.notes: Finasteride increases anagen hair in men with androgenetic alopecia.

effect_quant.comparator: placebo-adjusted difference in total hair count at 48 weeks

evidence.citation: OlsenEA et al 2014 J Am Acad Dermatol
evidence.notes: A randomized, active- and placebo-controlled study of the efficacy and safety of different doses of dutasteride versus placebo and finasteride in the treatment of male subjects with androgenetic alopecia.

evidence.citation: GuA et al 2024 J Cosmet Dermatol
evidence.notes: The impact of monotherapies for male androgenetic alopecia: A network meta-analysis study.
